Method of Attack: Malicious code embedded in two binary test files within the source code that targets the sshd process to bypass ssh authentication using glibc IFUNC calls, allowing unrestricted remote access
Encrypted code causing slow performance, hiding the backdoor
Impacted Systems: Operating systems distributing xz and liblzma packages (e.g., Fedora, Kali, unstable Debian releases)
Any Unix machine including macOS devices with any version of xz or liblzma installed
Containers and development machines using tools like homebrew
Attack Vector: Supply chain attack via malicious patches merged into the xz project repository by a trusted contributor (Jia Tan) through social engineering
Backdoor activated on systems using glibc and installed via .deb or .rpm packages
Indicators of Compromise: Slowed ssh login times (e.g., 500ms instead of 100ms)
Presence of malicious code in xz versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1
